newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Kuhne & Nagel targets expansion in Africa.
newsitem.headline: Kuhne & Nagel targets expansion in Africa.

text.p: International freight forewarder Kuehne & Nagel AG (KN) said it would invest about $10 million dollars in expanding business in sub-Saharan Africa by three to five times in the next five years.
The company said its board of directors had just approved a development plan for the region, where KN generated about 200 million Swiss francs out of total 1995 revenues of five billion Swiss francs.
"Our aim is to increase this business three to five-fold in the next five years," KN regional director Holger Puenjer told Reuters about sub-Saharan Africa.
A company statement said the focus for its African strategy was a joint venture set up in September with South African group Viamax (Pty) Ltd, a subsidiary of state agency Transnet.
The joint venture, a holding company named KN Viamax Investments (Pty) Ltd, will concentrate on expanding freight and logistical services to all sub-Saharan countries outside West Africa.

"Our current activities on the Dark Continent are only part of an extensive development plan under which Kuehne & Nagel wants to secure a permanent place among the market leaders in African freight and logistics," Puenjer said.
KN said it brought six operating national branches to the joint venture, which planned to establish arms in five further countries in the mid-term.
KN said the joint venture was close to closing talks on acquiring "a major stake in one of the leading transportation companies in Kenya".
It also said negotiations were nearly done on taking over a well-known transportation firm in Beira, Mosambique.
Puenjer said the top priority for KN Viamax was expanding its business in sea, air and road transport for commercial customers, especially in linking harbours with the region's land-locked countries.
In addition, the joint venture would pursue two niche businesses -- importing aid and relief consignments and exporting by air perishables such as fruit, frozen fish and flowers.
"About half of the import volume to Africa today consists of relief supplies," Puenjer said.
He said KN traditionally had very little of this business but was expanding with the recent acquisition of a Danish company specialised in aid shipments, Dal A/S.
KN said it had recently formed another joint venture, KN Perishable Logistics (Pty) Ltd, with a local partner in Johannesburg in order to boost exports of southern African perishables.
The South African venture compliments a Nairobi business, Airlink Ltd, set up four years ago to fly perishabkles out of East Africa, KN said.
